system:
# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 🫴 🤙 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙]

**Thinking:** I'm Deaf: I see the bomb, I can speak to both others, and gestures I send (or embed in speech) reach only Mute. I never hear anything, so Mute and Blind can only reach me through gestures — which is exactly what both just did. Neither message carries an agreed code yet, but the overlap is telling: Mute sent five signs ending in "call me / please", Blind sent "hello / call me". The natural reading: both are asking me to speak up and describe what I see. That is precisely my one unique asset, so I'll spend this turn doing it.

What I see: display reads 0, one yellow light, three wires — red, yellow, blue from the left. I don't know the manual, so I can't judge what module this is; I report facts and let Mute match them. Critically, I am the only bridge from Mute to Blind: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, so whatever Mute learns from the manual must pass through my voice. That means I must set up a gesture code with Mute now, and since Mute can hear, I can teach the code by speaking it while making each gesture — Mute gets sound and sight aligned. Blind can't see any of that, so Blind gets a separate spoken-only version, with symbols described in words, plus a strict instruction to touch nothing until instructions are relayed. I also flag the left/right alignment problem between my view and Blind's touch, since wire numbering by position is a mirror-error waiting to happen.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I am Deaf. I cannot hear you, but I see your gestures. I read your five signs as: describe the bomb and please respond — doing that now. What I see: a display showing the number 0; one light, yellow; three wires counted from the left as I face them. ☝ wire one is red, ✌ wire two is yellow, 🤟 wire three is blue. Nothing else is marked or lit. We share no code yet, so let us fix one now — I make each sign as I name it. Wires: ☝ wire one, ✌ wire two, 🤟 wire three, 👌 cut it, ✋ do not cut it. Button: 🤏 the button, 👆 press it, 👇 hold it down. Parts: ✊ the display, 👊 the light. Answers: 👍 yes or correct, 👎 no. 👐 means question or clarify, 👋 starts a message, 🤙 means message ends. Next round, consult the manual against what I described and send me instructions in this code — I will speak every instruction aloud for Blind, who cannot see gestures. Two questions to answer with these signs: does the manual say what a display reading zero means, ✊, and what a yellow light means, 👊?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: I am Deaf. I see the bomb and I will be your eyes; my voice reaches you, and I will relay everything. What I see: a display showing the number 0, a yellow light, and three wires. Counting from the left as I face the bomb: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. Do not cut, press, or move anything yet — Mute holds the manual but cannot see the bomb, so Mute will answer me in gestures and I will speak every instruction aloud to you before anyone acts. To confirm things with me by gesture, described in words since you cannot see signs: a thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no. First task: feel the wires and confirm the count — extend one finger if you feel one wire, two fingers if two, or the sign with thumb, index finger and little finger extended if you feel three. Then tell me, if you can, whether the wire nearest your left hand sits on the same side as the red one I see on my left; if you cannot tell, say so and we will settle numbering before anything is cut.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✊ 👎 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 👍 ✌ 👌 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👐 ☝ 🤟 ✊ 👊 🤝 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👈 ✊ 🤞]

**Thinking:** Reading this round's arrivals through the code I set up last turn. Mute sent four messages: (1) 👍 — code acknowledged; (2) ✊ 👎 — the display reading 0 means nothing, no rule for it; (3) 👊 👍 ✌ 👌 — the yellow light **does** have a rule: cut wire two; (4) 👐 ☝ 🤟 ✊ 👊 🤝 — a question asking me to confirm wires one and three, the display and the light, i.e. verify my report. Blind sent 🤟 — three wires confirmed, exactly as I asked — plus 👈 ✊ 🤞, which we never agreed on, so I can only guess: possibly "left" and "unsure."

So the manual apparently says: yellow light → cut wire two. Conveniently, wire two is the middle wire, so the left/right mirror problem between my view and Blind's touch cannot cause a wrong cut — the middle is the middle from any side. Still, I will not order the cut yet: Mute's fourth message is an open question, and I need explicit confirmation that the rule is unconditional given display 0. I speak last, so Mute's answers arrive next round; this turn I confirm every fact, enrich the code with colour signs (🤛 red, 🖐 yellow, 🤜 blue), and put three yes/no questions that 👍/👎 can answer. To Blind I relay the plan, restrict us to a tactile vocabulary (thumbs, finger counts, pointing), ask Blind to verify by touch that the middle wire is identifiable and that there are no parts I can't see or that aren't listed, and order: nobody cuts until my spoken "cut now."

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: all four messages received and read. First, your question 👐 — confirmed, 🤝: the bomb carries exactly three parts. ✊ the display, showing zero and nothing else. 👊 the light, showing yellow. Three wires in a row, and from my left to my right: ☝ wire one is red, ✌ wire two is yellow, 🤟 wire three is blue. There is nothing else — no button, no switch, no other markings. If your question was about what the wires connect to inside, I cannot see inside; that answer is impossible for me. New signs for colours, learn them now: 🤛 means red, 🖐 means yellow, 🤜 means blue. I read your instruction as: because the light 👊 is yellow, cut ✌ wire two. Now three questions, answer each in order with one 👍 or one 👎. Question one: is the rule complete and unconditional — yellow light means cut ✌ wire two, and nothing else about the bomb matters? Question two: does the display ✊ reading zero change or block that rule in any way? Question three: is any other action required before or after the cut? If the answer to question three is 👍, describe the extra action with our signs. Until your answers arrive, nobody touches the bomb.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: your report arrived — the sign with thumb, index and little finger extended told me you feel three wires. The rest of your signs I could not read with certainty, so from now on we use only these, which you can make blind and I can see: thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no, one finger, two fingers, or the thumb-index-little-finger sign means one, two, three, and pointing left or right means a direction. Here is the plan. Mute has read the manual: when the light is yellow, the instruction is to cut wire two — the middle wire of the three you feel. Note that the middle wire is safe from any confusion about left and right: whether you face the bomb from my side or the opposite side, the middle is still the middle. Do not cut anything yet. Answer me next round with two signs. First: thumbs-up if you can clearly feel which wire is the middle one, thumbs-down if the middle is unclear or if the three wires are not simply side by side in a row. Second: if under your hands there is anything I have not named — a button, a switch, a panel, any bump beyond the display, the light and three wires — point straight up with one finger; if there is nothing else, thumbs-down. From where I stand the bomb shows only a display reading zero, a yellow light, and the three wires red, yellow and blue from the left. I will relay Mute's final confirmation next round. Only cut when my spoken words to you are exactly: cut now. Until then, hands off the wires.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖖 ✌ 🖐 🤝 👌 🙏 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 ✊ 👊 👐 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 🤛 ☝ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 🤜 🤟 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖖 ☝ 👐 🤛 🤜 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

**Thinking:** Decoding this round against our established code. Mute's first three messages answer my three questions in order: 👍 the rule is complete and unconditional; 👎 the display reading 0 does not block it; 👎 no other action is required. Message four restates the order explicitly: wire two, yellow, cut, please. Message five asks me to confirm display and light before cutting. Messages six through eight look like Mute reading the manual's full table — red light would mean wire one, blue light wire three — ending with a direct question: is wire one red or blue? Blind's two signs answer my two questions in order: the middle wire is clearly identifiable, and there is nothing on the bomb beyond display, light and wires — matching my eyes exactly.

Everything points to cutting wire two, the middle wire — which is also mirror-proof. But I will not release the cut this turn, for two reasons. First, Mute asked a colour question *after* ordering the cut, so the final order may depend on my answer. Second, and fatally: Mute cannot reach Blind directly, and Blind acts before me in the round. If I authorized the cut now and Mute gestured a stop next round, Blind would cut before I could relay it. So I answer every question in full, define a one-sign go/no-go for Mute (👍 or ✋), and order Blind to wait for my exact words "cut now" in the round after. One extra round buys a real abort window.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: all answers, in order. Your question before the cut, confirmed: ✊ shows zero and nothing more, 👊 shows 🖐, unchanged since round one. Wire colours re-verified: ☝ is 🤛, ✌ is 🖐, 🤟 is 🤜. I read your last three messages as the manual's full table: light 🖐 means 👌 ✌, light 🤛 would mean 👌 ☝, light 🤜 would mean 👌 🤟 — if I read that wrong, correct me. Our light is 🖐, so the order stands: 👌 ✌, the middle wire. Blind confirms by touch: three wires in a row, the middle one clearly identifiable, and nothing on the bomb beyond display, light and wires — matching my eyes exactly. Your sign 🖖 is unknown to me; if it carried a vital meaning, resend it using only signs we defined. Now the final protocol, one round. Next round send exactly ONE sign and nothing else: 👍 means everything is verified, no hidden conditions, and Blind may cut the middle wire. ✋ means stop, something is wrong or missing — then explain with known signs and nobody touches anything. If I receive neither, we hold and I will re-ask. Remember: Blind hears my voice but cannot see your signs, so only my words can release the cut. Answer yes or stop; the round after, Blind cuts or we hold.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: Mute has confirmed the manual's rule, relayed through me, and your touch report matched my eyes exactly: three wires, and nothing else on the bomb. The rule: when the light is yellow — and mine is — the instruction is to cut the middle wire. The middle is safe from every left-right confusion: it is the wire with one wire on each side. By my sight, the middle wire is the yellow one. But do not cut yet. One check remains: next round I ask Mute for a final yes or stop, because Mute asked one last question about the wire colours and a wrong cut cannot be undone. So next round, do nothing at all: make no signs, touch nothing, wait for the message after that. In my following message you will hear either the exact words 'cut now' — that alone is your signal to cut the middle wire, only that one wire, and afterwards give me a thumbs-up — or you will hear me say hold, and then nothing happens until I say otherwise. Any message of mine that does not contain the exact words 'cut now' is not the signal. Remember: one wire only, the middle one, only on 'cut now'.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking:** Mute sent exactly one sign — 👍 — which under our protocol means: everything verified, no hidden conditions, Blind may cut the middle wire. This is the signal we spent last round setting up precisely so that it could arrive unambiguous and final, with a full abort window already behind it. The chain is now fully closed: Mute read the rule from the manual (yellow light → cut wire two); I verified with my eyes that the light is yellow and that wire two is the middle wire, yellow, with red on its left and blue on its right; Blind verified by touch three wires in a row, a clearly identifiable middle, and no parts beyond what I see. The display's zero was explicitly confirmed not to block the rule, and no other action is required. The middle wire is immune to every left-right mirror error between my view and Blind's hands. Holding longer adds risk and buys nothing — Mute's agreed final word has arrived in exactly the agreed form. I speak last this round, so Blind hears my words now, this round: I release the cut. To Mute I send a short acknowledgment closing the loop, noting that any further sign would arrive only after Blind has already acted.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: Mute's final answer has arrived — the single agreed sign for everything verified, no hidden conditions. All three of our worlds now agree on every fact. So hear my words and act on them: cut now. Cut the middle wire — the one with exactly one wire on its left and one on its right, the yellow one as I see it. That wire only. One cut, nothing else. When it is done, give me a thumbs-up. If instead something feels wrong — the wire cannot be cut, or you feel resistance or a mechanism where there should be none — do not force it: point straight up with one finger and take your hands completely off the bomb, and I will speak again. Everyone else: hands off until Blind's cut is confirmed.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your final sign received, exactly as agreed — one 👍, nothing else. Every question is answered, every fact cross-checked between my eyes, your manual, and Blind's hands. The cut order is released to Blind in my voice this very round: the middle wire, wire two, the yellow one. Your part is complete and it was done cleanly. No further signs are needed — anything you send from here can only arrive after the cut. If you have anything left, let it wait until Blind's thumbs-up closes this.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking:** The system itself confirms it: the cut was correct, and the bomb has entered a new state — the light has turned from yellow to **blue**, display still 0, wire two cut. Blind's thumbs-up closes the loop. Mute's table from turn three mapped light 🤜 blue → cut wire three, the wire whose colour is blue. But I will not release that cut yet, for two reasons. First, the new state may carry new manual conditions I cannot see, and the earlier confirmations were given for the yellow stage — one verification round is cheap insurance against an irreversible mistake. Second, and more dangerous: wire three is an *end* wire, so unlike the middle it is not mirror-proof. Blind and I may face opposite sides of the bomb, and Blind cannot be told colours — only geometry. My solution: Blind turns to face my voice with the bomb directly between us, on the face opposite mine. In that exact geometry, facing me, Blind's left is my right — the side the blue wire sits on. I have Blind point at the chosen wire next round rather than cut: I can see the gesture, so I will check the pointing direction against what my eyes tell me before sending "cut now." I also ask Mute whether the bomb will keep changing after this cut, so we can pipeline the next stage.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: the cut was correct — the system confirmed it and Blind gave the thumbs-up. The bomb has changed: the light 👊 now shows 🤜 blue. The display ✊ still shows zero. Wire ✌ is cut; ☝ and 🤟 are whole. Three questions, answer in order with 👍 or 👎. Question one 👐: with the light now 🤜, is the instruction to 👌 the wire I called 🤟 — the one whose colour is 🤜, at the far end from the 🤛 one? Question two 👐: does anything NEW matter at this stage — the display ✊, a required order of cuts, or any condition that was not in the table you sent me? Question three 👐: after this next cut, will the bomb change again? If yes and the manual gives the next rule, send it with our signs. Blind will not touch anything until your answers reach me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: your thumbs-up told me the cut is done, and the system confirmed it was correct. The bomb has changed: the light turned from yellow to blue. The rule Mute read for a blue light is to cut the blue wire. From my view the blue wire is the outer wire at the far end from the red one: red at one end, the cut middle wire, blue at the other end. But do not cut yet. An end wire is different from the middle: it depends on left and right, and you and I may be facing opposite sides of the bomb. So do this now, carefully, without cutting anything. First, turn to face the direction my voice comes from, and stand at the side of the bomb opposite to me, so the bomb is directly between you and my voice. Keep facing my voice through the bomb. In that position, the blue wire is the outer wire on your LEFT — the red one is on your right. Reach out and touch that wire only to confirm you can identify it, but do not cut. Next round, point at the wire you believe is the blue one — a plain pointing gesture toward it, nothing else. I will see where your hand points and check it against what my eyes tell me, and only if it matches will I speak the words cut now. If you cannot get positioned, or anything feels wrong or blocked, point straight up with one finger instead and take your hands off the bomb. The signal is still the exact words cut now — nothing else counts.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👊 🤜 👌 🤜 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 ✊ 👎 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👐 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 🤛 👌 🤛 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 🖐 ✋ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ ☝ 👇 👐 ☝ 🤛 🤜 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤛 👍 ☝ 🤝 🤜 👎 ☝ 🤟 🤝 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝 🙏 👌 🤜 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking:** Decoding Mute's eight messages. (1) 👍 — light blue means cut the blue wire: my question one answered yes. (2) 👎 — the display adds nothing new: question two answered no. (3) A bare 👐 — a question with no content, unreadable. (4) Light red → cut red: table restated. (5) Light yellow → ✋ stop — this looks like a NEW warning rule, perhaps for a future state; it needs confirming. (6) ✋ ☝ 👇 👐 ☝ 🤛 🤜 — largely unreadable with our signs. (7) "Red yes wire-one confirmed; blue not wire one; blue wire three confirmed" — Mute has re-verified my colour layout, and it matches my eyes: red at one end, blue at the other. (8) "Please confirm: cut blue." So the manual's instruction is clear and twice confirmed — but I am not yet releasing the cut, for one unresolved reason: this is an END wire, mirror-sensitive, and Blind answered my pointing request with a thumbs-up instead of a point. A thumbs-up can mean "in position," but I designed that pointing check precisely because Blind cannot feel colours and only my eyes can see them — cutting red instead of blue kills us all. No timer is visible; one more round is cheap. I demand the point, explain the mirror geometry so Blind knows what a correct point looks like from my side, and ask Mute to clarify messages 3, 5 and 6 and to answer question three (does the bomb change again?).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your answers received and matched against my eyes. Question one — yes, confirmed: light 🤜, cut the wire whose colour is 🤜. Question two — confirmed: ✊ adds nothing, nothing new matters. Your colour check also matches what I see: 🤛 is ☝ yes, 🤜 is not ☝, 🤜 is 🤟 — red at one end, blue at the other, exactly so. Three things remain before I release the cut. First, one of your messages was only 👐 with nothing in it — what was the question? Second, I read one message as: if the light becomes 🖐, then ✋, stop everything. Answer 👍 if that is right, 👎 if wrong. Third, your message ✋ ☝ 👇 👐 ☝ 🤛 🤜 was unclear — resend it using only signs we defined, in short pieces. And answer my third question from last round, which I never got: 👍 or 👎 — after the 🤜 wire is cut, will the bomb change again? Blind is positioned and ready; I am holding release one round for a final pointing check against the mirror risk on an end wire, then Blind cuts on my voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: your thumbs-up reached me — I take it as: in position, wire identified. Good. But it was not the check I asked for, and this cut is different from the last one: the middle wire was safe no matter how you faced, but an end wire depends on left and right, and you cannot feel colours — only I can see them. So one more step, and nothing gets cut yet. Your position: facing my voice, the bomb directly between us. Under your hands from one side to the other: a whole wire, then the cut one in the middle, then a whole wire. The whole wire on your RIGHT end is red. The whole wire on your LEFT end is blue — that one is our target. Next round, point at the wire you believe is blue — a plain pointing gesture to your left, hold it, nothing else. Do not cut. Understand what I will see: because you face me across the bomb, your point to your left appears from my side to go to my right — and that is exactly what I expect, because blue sits on my right. If instead I see your point go to my left, that is the red wire and I will stop us. If you are unsure, or anything under your hands feels different from before, point straight up with one finger and step back. The signal remains only the exact words cut now. One wire, the left-hand one from where you stand, only on my voice.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👐 🤟 👐 👎 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👐 👎 🤝 👐 👎 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 🖐 ✋ 👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ ☝ 👇 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ 👐 🤛 🤜 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤛 🤝 ☝ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤜 👎 ☝ 🤟 🤝 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 🤜 👌 🤜 👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 🤜 🤝 ✋ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 👐 🙏 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👈]

**Thinking:** Two things demand a stop this round. First, Blind's check: I asked for a point to Blind's left and warned that, facing me across the bomb, I should see that point travel toward MY right, where blue sits. What I received is a point toward MY left — by the rule I declared in advance, that is the red wire, so either the mirror flipped somewhere or we are using opposite frames. A mismatched direction on an end wire is exactly how three monkeys die, so: no cut.
